pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which interjection fits a small mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Wow
   B. Oops
   C. Bravo
   D. Hurray

2. Which feeling does Ouch! show? (1 mark)
   A. Joy
   B. Disgust
   C. Pain
   D. Sleepiness

3. Which is a constructive leisure activity? (1 mark)
   A. Harming others
   B. Fighting
   C. Wasting money
   D. Reading a book

4. How should notes be written? (1 mark)
   A. As whole paragraphs
   B. As short phrases of key words
   C. As drawings only
   D. As long sentences

5. What is the main idea of a passage? (1 mark)
   A. The page number
   B. The last word
   C. The date
   D. What it is mostly about

6. What is a singing game with interjections? (1 mark)
   A. A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   B. A silent game
   C. A story
   D. A written test

7. Which is a mistake in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Using a full stop
   B. Using a question
   C. Using a name
   D. Forgetting the colon after the name

8. What is role play? (1 mark)
   A. Acting out a situation
   B. Drawing only
   C. Copying
   D. Reading silently

9. Which sentence uses an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. On the table.
   B. The heavy computer is on the table.
   C. The computer is on.
   D. Computers work.

10. Which adjective describes colour? (1 mark)
   A. silver
   B. large
   C. tall
   D. thin

11. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A poem
   B. A time
   C. A thing made or grown for sale
   D. A place

12. What is an advertisement? (1 mark)
   A. A message that tells about a product or service to attract buyers
   B. A lesson
   C. A poem
   D. A weather report

13. Which field asks how old you are? (1 mark)
   A. Signature
   B. School
   C. Age
   D. Class

14. What does a good form have? (1 mark)
   A. Tiny words only
   B. No spaces
   C. No title
   D. Clear title, instructions and enough space

15. What is polite when you want to speak in a discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Stand on a chair
   B. Shout
   C. Raise your hand or signal
   D. Snatch the talking stick

16. What is a panel discussion? (1 mark)
   A. A solo song
   B. A quiz
   C. A game of football
   D. A planned discussion by a small group before an audience

17. What is repetition in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Deleting lines
   B. Changing the title
   C. Repeating words or lines for effect
   D. Adding a picture

18. Which is the first step in understanding a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Copy it
   B. Read the title and the poem aloud
   C. Tear it
   D. Ignore it

19. Which is a signal word for the second step? (1 mark)
   A. Yesterday
   B. Finally
   C. Next
   D. Never

20. In writing, what is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A poem
   B. Words telling someone what to do
   C. A picture
   D. A story

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Name two components of a poem. (2 marks)

22. Give two adjectives to describe a mobile phone. (2 marks)

23. Write a short telephone conversation of six lines between a pupil and a friend about homework. Use polite expressions. (5 marks)

24. Explain two differences between an advert and a news item. (4 marks)

25. Give two examples of constructive leisure activities. (2 marks)

26. Create a form with four fields to find out classmates' favourite games. Include a title and instructions. (4 marks)

27. Explain what turn taking means. (2 marks)

28. Explain what a stanza is. (2 marks)

29. Give two adjectives to describe a school bag in an advert. (2 marks)

30. Explain what an interjection is and give two examples. (2 marks)

31. Give three rules for good turn taking. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

2. C — Pain
   People say ouch when hurt.

3. D — Reading a book
   Constructive activities build people up.

4. B — As short phrases of key words
   Notes are brief.

5. D — What it is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

6. A — A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   Interjections can be part of songs.

7. D — Forgetting the colon after the name
   The colon is needed after the name.

8. A — Acting out a situation
   Role play acts a scene.

9. B — The heavy computer is on the table.
   Heavy describes the computer.

10. A — silver
   Silver is a colour.

11. C — A thing made or grown for sale
   A product is a thing for sale.

12. A — A message that tells about a product or service to attract buyers
   Adverts promote products or services.

13. C — Age
   Age records how old you are.

14. D — Clear title, instructions and enough space
   Clarity makes forms easy to fill.

15. C — Raise your hand or signal
   Signal politely.

16. D — A planned discussion by a small group before an audience
   A panel discusses a topic.

17. C — Repeating words or lines for effect
   Repetition emphasises an idea.

18. B — Read the title and the poem aloud
   Reading aloud comes first.

19. C — Next
   Next shows the following step.

20. B — Words telling someone what to do
   Instructions say what to do.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, message (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: small, black, thin, new, flat (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible adjective.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any six lines with greeting, name, reason, polite words, thanks and goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for greeting, one for giving names, one for the reason, one for polite words, one for thanks and goodbye.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: An advert aims to persuade people to buy, while news informs about events. An advert gives a price and where to buy, while news gives who, what, where and when.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for each difference.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reading, sports, drawing, singing, gardening, community service (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Title: Favourite Games. Instructions: Write neatly. Fields: Name, Class, Favourite game, Date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for title, one for instructions, two for four fields.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means speaking one person at a time and waiting for others to finish before speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for one at a time and one for waiting.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem, separated from the next group by a space.
   Working / marking points: One mark for group of lines and one for separation.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: strong, big, red, light, new (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each adjective.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: An interjection is a short word or sound showing sudden feeling, for example Wow and Ouch.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for two examples.

31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wait for the speaker to finish, keep your turn short, do not always speak first, listen politely.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.
